questions.questionText: What is the main role of the Structured Concurrency model in Swift?

possibleAnswers.optionText: To ensure child tasks are automatically cancelled when their parent task is cancelled
To force all tasks to execute on the main thread in a predictable order
To manage memory allocation between synchronous and asynchronous calls
To serialize access to global shared state across tasks

questions.questionText: What is the difference between Task.detached and Task.init in Swift?

possibleAnswers.optionText: Task.detached runs outside the current actor context, while Task.init inherits it
Task.detached is always higher priority than Task.init
Task.init is cancelled immediately if detached tasks fail
Task.detached can only run on the main thread, while Task.init can run anywhere

questions.questionText: How does an AsyncSequence differ from a regular Sequence in Swift?

possibleAnswers.optionText: AsyncSequence produces elements asynchronously over time using await
AsyncSequence stores all its values in memory before iteration begins
AsyncSequence guarantees results will always be delivered on the main actor
AsyncSequence requires values to conform to Sendable by default

questions.questionText: What happens if you call await inside a non-async function?

possibleAnswers.optionText: It results in a compiler error because await requires an async context
The function will implicitly be promoted to async by the compiler
The function will run synchronously but block the main thread
It compiles, but execution is delayed until the enclosing actor finishes

questions.questionText: What is the role of withTaskGroup in Swift concurrency?

possibleAnswers.optionText: It allows creation and coordination of dynamically created child tasks
It ensures that all async calls execute on a single actor
It runs all tasks sequentially and returns after each completion
It prevents cancellation from propagating to child tasks

questions.questionText: How are priority values like .high and .background used in Swift concurrency?

possibleAnswers.optionText: They influence task scheduling, but do not guarantee execution order
They guarantee higher-priority tasks will always complete first
They determine which actor executes the associated tasks
They prevent tasks from being cancelled once started

questions.questionText: What is the role of MainActor in Swift concurrency?

possibleAnswers.optionText: It isolates tasks to the main thread for UI-related operations
It guarantees that code executes with the highest possible priority
It prevents async functions from suspending while awaiting results
It manages structured concurrency across detached tasks

questions.questionText: How does try? interact with async/await in Swift?

possibleAnswers.optionText: It converts thrown errors into nil even when used with await
It automatically retries failed async calls before returning
It forces the task to run synchronously in error cases
It wraps results into a Result type automatically

questions.questionText: What is the main difference between actor and class in Swift?

possibleAnswers.optionText: Actor ensures isolated access to its mutable state, class does not
Actor cannot contain stored properties, class can
Actor cannot inherit from other actors, class can inherit freely
Actor properties are always immutable, class properties can be mutable

questions.questionText: What is the default behaviour if a child task inside withTaskGroup throws?

possibleAnswers.optionText: The error propagates out of the group and cancels remaining tasks
The error is ignored and only successful results are returned
The group retries the failing child task until success
The parent task continues unaffected while child tasks complete
